newsitem.title: JAPAN: Retailer's earnings hurt by mad cows and germs.
newsitem.headline: Retailer's earnings hurt by mad cows and germs.

text.p: A food poisoning epidemic and fears over mad-cow disease on Wednesday forced Yaohan Japan Corp, a core member of international retailer Yaohan group, to sharply cut its earnings forecast for the current business year.

"Amid increasingly intensified competition due to deregulation, we expect our sales to be lower than we previously estimated because of (worries over) mad-cow disease and the O-157 colon bacillus," Yaohan Japan said in a statement.
It also said that sales of summer clothing were slow.
Yaohan Japan is one of the four core companies of the Yaohan group which is actively expanding business overseas, especially in China in the past few years. Yaohan Japan runs outlets in Japan.
Yaohan Japan lowered its parent current profit forecast for the six months to September 30 to 1.06 billion yen ($9.5 million) from its previous forecast of 2.01 billion yen ($18.1 million).

Yaohan Japan also revised down its parent current profit forecast for the full 1996/97 business year to March 31, 1997, to 2.68 billion yen ($24.1 million), down from its earlier forecast of 4.32 billion yen ($38.9 million). In 1995/96, Yaohan's actual parent current profit was 4.65 billion yen ($41.8 million).
Current profit is pre-tax and includes gains and losses made on securities investments and other non-operating activities.

Sales of beef and other food items fell at Japanese retailers and supermarkets earlier this year due to a widespread food poisoning epidemic caused by the O-157 strain of the E. coli bacteria and worries over a potential link between bovine spongiform encephalopathy, commonly called mad-cow disease, and its human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.
The O-157 strain, which causes severe diarrhoea, vomiting and fevers that often lead to liver complications, killed 11 people and made more than 9,500 people ill so far this year in Japan.
Due to the fall in profits, Yaohan Japan cut its interim dividend to 4.50 yen from its previous estimate of 8.25 yen.
